title: Induction of Anemia and RBC Transfusion–associated Necrotizing Enterocolitis in Neonatal Mice
author: Balamurugan Ramatchandirin

steps.title: Collect whole blood and add CPDA‑1
steps.instruction: One week before transfusion, anesthetize an adult FVB/NJ donor mouse with isoflurane (1.5%–2.5%) in an induction box until non‑responsive, apply 0.5% proparacaine ophthalmic solution 5 min before retro‑orbital bleeding, hold the mouse by the neck skin, puncture the medial canthus with a heparinized (or non‑heparinized) capillary tube, collect 860 µL whole blood, immediately add 140 µL CPDA‑1 (final 14% v/v) in a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube to make 1 mL total, and euthanize the mouse according to IACUC policy.

steps.title: Leukoreduce and store packed RBCs
steps.instruction: Filter the freshly collected blood through a sterile Acrodisc WBC syringe filter, centrifuge the leukoreduced blood at 295 × g for 10 min, remove supernatant until the hematocrit is ≈75%, aliquot 500 µL portions into sterile 1.5 mL tubes leaving a small air space, and store the tubes in the dark at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare Serratia marcescens culture
steps.instruction: Three days before transfusion, scrape ~10 µL of a frozen S. marcescens glycerol stock with a sterile pipette tip, add it to 10 mL LB broth in a 15 mL culture tube, and incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 37 °C, 150 rpm in an orbital shaker; include a parallel tube with sterile LB as a contamination control. Measure OD₆₀₀ of the culture; adjust with sterile LB so the OD₆₀₀ is 0.6 ± 0.02 (dilute if higher, continue culturing if lower). Transfer 2 mL of the adjusted culture to a 2 mL centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the bacterial pellet in 1 mL sterile PBS for oral gavage.

steps.title: Induce phlebotomy‑induced anemia (P1‑P10)
steps.instruction: From post‑natal day 1 (P1) to P10, weigh each pup and assign to anemic or control groups. For anemic pups, grasp the loose neck skin, perform facial‑vein phlebotomy to withdraw 10 µL of blood per gram body weight, and immediately inject an equal volume of 0.9 % NaCl intraperitoneally using a 30 G needle attached to a 0.5 mL syringe; for control pups, prick the scruff with a needle without drawing blood to match handling stress. Repeat the procedure daily, monitoring hematocrit with a Sysmex XN‑1000 analyzer and observing for pallor. For pups older than P5, warm under lights for 5 min before phlebotomy to dilate veins.

steps.title: Oral gavage of S. marcescens (P7)
steps.instruction: On post‑natal day 7, fill a 1 mL syringe with the S. marcescens suspension, attach a 3.5 French (0.35 mm) Umbili‑cath polyurethane UVC catheter, gently grasp the pup’s neck skin, insert the catheter 2 cm into the oropharynx/esophagus without resistance, slowly dispense 50 µL (≈10⁴ CFU) into the stomach, withdraw the catheter, and monitor for respiratory distress or emesis.

steps.title: Transfuse stored RBCs via orbital sinus (P11)
steps.instruction: On post‑natal day 11, bring stored RBC aliquots to room temperature and gently resuspend by rotating. Using a 31 G, 0.3125 in needle attached to a 0.3 mL insulin syringe, clean the area above the eye with sterile saline and a cotton‑tipped applicator (no alcohol or ophthalmic anesthetic). Restrain the pup in left lateral recumbency (right‑handed) or opposite for left‑handed staff, insert the needle bevel‑down at the 3 o’clock position into the medial canthus at ~30° angle, and inject ≤50 µL of the RBC suspension in a smooth motion. Optionally, inject Trypan blue in separate pups to confirm systemic circulation. Withdraw the needle slowly, clean any bleed with a cotton applicator, place the pup in a prepared nest, check for additional bleeding, and return the pup to its dam.

steps.title: Assess hematocrit and collect samples (P12)
steps.instruction: Immediately after the P11 transfusion, measure hematocrit with the Sysmex XN‑1000 analyzer; on P12, sacrifice pups according to institutional guidelines, collect blood and intestinal tissues, and process the plasma for intestinal fatty‑acid‑binding protein 2 (iFABP2) ELISA using the commercial kit (linear range 78–5,000 pg/mL) per manufacturer instructions; also fix intestinal sections for histopathology (H&E) to evaluate NEC lesions.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article(s): MohanKumar, K. et al. (2019). A murine neonatal model of necrotizing enterocolitis caused by anemia and red blood cell transfusions. Nature Communication.
